articles.title: Weather on the board today
articles.body:
A dense high-pressure system of caste geometry dominated the morning, as Anon argued over whether the inch measures 130 or 76.

The barometric readings were heavy, with the weight of the debate pressing down on the board like a thick, unmoving overcast.

No fronts broke through the haze of mathematical dispute, leaving the atmosphere stagnant and thick with unresolved numerology. Beneath that ceiling, a scattered squall of Jaat braggadocio rolled through the afternoon.

Claims of genital supremacy and sassy Pahdi dialect kept the temperature low and the visibility poor.

The drizzle was persistent, mixing with a cold snap of railway worker melancholy that seeped in from the plains, complaining of potholes and pollution.

It was a soggy, grey day, with only the dry, static hum of radio updates providing a brief moment of clear air.

articles.title: The Geometry of the Abbo
articles.body:
Anon posted a puzzle asking the board to identify the odd one out among five shapes, specifically requesting to see if the correct answer was 130 or 76. The image presented a grid of squares and circles with varying sizes, colors, and borders.

The immediate response from the board was not a calculation of areas but a swift classification of the respondent's caste and intelligence. One Anon argued for the fourth object, citing it as the only borderless square among red shapes.

Another Anon dismissed this approach as overcomplication, claiming that trying to find patterns where none exist was a sign of youthful foolishness. The majority of the thread, however, coalesced around the second object.

Multiple posters argued that the second shape was the odd one out because it shared common characteristics with the rest, making it the only one that did not stand out in a specific way.

The justification for choosing the second object quickly devolved into a test of social hierarchy. One Anon stated that answering two correctly meant the user had an average IQ, while any other answer indicated a low abbo IQ.

This provoked a defensive reply from an Anon who identified as an abbo, claiming that most of the others who missed the answer were northie khetshitters.

The thread became a mirror in which Anons saw their own rural or urban biases reflected in their geometric choices. Accusations of stupidity were exchanged with little regard for the actual puzzle logic.

One respondent was told that sitting on a western toilet had caused constipation, preventing them from thinking outside the obvious. This was met with a correction that IQ tests measure pattern recognition and processing speed, not a single riddle.

Another Anon noted that answering correctly did not prove high IQ, only that the person was a midwit abbo compared to a dimwit abbo who missed it.

The debate shifted from the properties of the shapes to the properties of the typists, with one poster mocking the spelling of a respondent who wrote 'u' and 'ur' instead of 'you' and 'your'.

Despite the insults, the logical core of the argument remained that the second shape was the only one with something in common with all others.

One Anon pointed out that any other shape had a differing quality that no other shape shared, whereas the second had no such unique distinctness.

The board spent more time debating who was an abbo and who was a northie than they did analyzing the borders of the squares.

The puzzle served less as a test of cognitive ability and more as a litmus test for regional prejudice on Indiachan.

articles.title: Anon Claims Jaat Genitals Are Superior to BJP
articles.body:
Anon opened a thread with the text "BIG JAAT PENIS" and a claim that BBC is supreme.

He stated that anyone complaining about size, including members of BDL, BJP, and other groups, is merely coping and should accept the superiority of the Jaat phallus.

The first respondent accused Anon of spamming the board with this content. Another Anon replied that he was not spamming, adding that he only posted in response to others complaining about size.

A third Anon asked for evidence of the claim, prompting the OP to admit he had none but insisted that everyone who interacted with him would subconsciously learn of the BBC's supremacy. Further replies intensified the personal attacks.

One Anon called the OP a faggot who kept other men's genitals in his phone. Another noted that the videos Anon posted contained only plastic black dildos, not real content.

The OP responded by calling the accusers boring and confirming that he had never spammed, attributing his behavior to an "autismo thing" where he posts only when bored or provoked. The thread devolved into caste-based insults.

One Anon identified himself as an OBC-NC Shudra and claimed his own genitals were fairer than the BBC. Others labeled participants as Bihari Kayasthas and black bhangers.

One Anon offered to give his Rajput sister to the OP for breeding, which was met with a request for the pair to get a room.

articles.title: Phahdi Sassing and Jat Lingo
articles.body:
Anon opened the thread by mocking a Pahadi girl for displaying her "chad lite" Jat boyfriend, calling the union "gobari daa." The replies immediately devolved into a technical dispute over board mechanics.

One Anon accused the OP of being a NEET who did not understand that imageboards lack page numbers, while another defended the original post's position on the board.

The exchange grew foul, with posters trading insults about being "low iq" and "shudras" and questioning the cognitive bandwidth required to post a single reply. A separate faction focused on physical measurements.

Anon estimated the girl's height at 5'7 or 5'8, while the boyfriend was pegged at just 6 feet. Another user claimed to be a Himachali with a Jat girlfriend, asserting the female partner was 5'6 against his own 5'11.

One anon simply stated he was at the same Punjab college as the couple, refusing to engage with the height speculation. The thread then fractured over the nomenclature of Jat women.

Anon claimed Sikh Jat women call themselves "jatti" while Hindu Jat women use "jatni." This triggered a heated argument about regional accuracy, with one user berating another as a "pahadhaggu" for claiming Sikh Jats use the latter term.

The dispute escalated into personal attacks, including crude threats involving family members. Amidst the caste-based slurs and height debates, one Anon expressed indifference to the "stacyjeeta" aesthetic, preferring partners who did not look like bimbos.

Another user dismissed the entire argument as "torsissy" malding, laughing at the intensity of the conflict.

The thread ended without resolution, leaving the height of the boyfriend, the correct dialect for Jat women, and the social standing of the Pahadi girl all equally unverified.

articles.title: IAC Radio Updates and Forum Usage
articles.body:
Anon asked the board how they were liking the new radio setup, noting that the host's talk duration was adjusted to three to four minutes between songs to report on news more concretely.

The poster also highlighted new animations that replaced simple buttons, which they described as a good screensave.

One respondent asked if the OP was a night owl or living in a different time zone, questioning why they only posted so late at night. The OP replied that they were currently living in Vilayat.

Another anon asked for a definition of the word "vilayat" after seeing the response. The OP also mentioned seeing folks actually using the IAC forum and asked if those users wanted any visual changes, confirming the forum is open to all.

articles.title: Railway Worker Laments Plain Life
articles.body:
An anon complained that his father should have migrated from the plains to a hilly area, citing pollution, pootholes, and noise as reasons for the move. Another anon asked for app ideas that would generate infinite money to fund such a relocation.

A respondent called the OP a "bimarpoos" and claimed mountains were only for "Aryan bulls." The OP clarified that his father is a railway government employee.

One user suggested getting a job in the mountain area, while another asked what kind of job that would be.
